question: How does Percival get even with O'Gallagher after he takes all of the boy's fireworks?
gold: He sets them on fire with the teacher sitting on them
final_answer:
Percival sneaks back into the empty schoolroom, lifts the claret case under which O’Gallagher has hidden the confiscated squibs and crackers, and packs additional gunpowder under it—leaving only a tiny, hard-to-notice train in the green baize.  

When O’Gallagher sits back down on the “throne,” Percival lights the train with touchwood, setting off the stored fireworks and powder so that the claret case blasts upward and O’Gallagher is “thrown up to the ceiling” in a cloud of smoke while the crackers and squibs fizz and bang (and the schoolroom catches fire).

question: How does Chuck end up on an island?
gold: His plane crashes and his life raft washes up on an island.
final_answer: Chuck ends up on the island because the FedEx cargo plane he’s on plummets out of the sky and crashes into the Pacific during a storm. In the wreck, his life jacket is inflated and he survives in the water as the plane sinks; afterward he’s carried by the waves and washes up on a beach (found face-down/partly buried in the sand), which is the island.

question: Why does Mr. Hardcastle want his daughter to meet Charles Marlow?
final_answer: Mr. Hardcastle wants his daughter to meet Charles Marlow because he has “pitched upon” Marlow as a suitable match: Marlow is “the son of my old friend, Sir Charles Marlow,” and Hardcastle has heard he is well educated (“bred a scholar”), intended for public service, and “a man of an excellent understanding.”

output.summary: The Lady Lorna Dugal is gone, because she could not help herself; and she wept enough to break ten hearts--if hearts are ever broken, John." "Darling Lizzie, how good you are!" I cried, without noticing her sneer; "tell me all about it, dear; tell me every word she said." "That will not take long," said Lizzie, quite as unmoved by soft coaxing as by urgent cursing; "the lady spoke very little to any one, except indeed to mother, and to Gwenny Carfax; and Gwenny is gone with her, so that the benefit of that is lost. Who will thresh it out of you, and starve it, and swear it out of you!" was the meaning of my imprecation: but Lizzie, not dreaming as yet of such things, could not understand me, and was rather thankful; therefore she answered quietly,-- "The letter is in the little cupboard, near the head of Lady Lorna's bed, where she used to keep the diamond necklace, which we contrived to get stolen." Without another word I rushed (so that every board in the house shook) up to my lost Lorna's room, and tore the little wall-niche open and espied my treasure. Though they tell you I am false, though your own mind harbours it, from the sense of things around, and your own undervaluing, yet take counsel of your heart, and cast such thoughts away from you; being unworthy of itself they must be unworthy also of the one who dwells there; and that one is, and ever shall be, your own Lorna Dugal." Some people cannot understand that tears should come from pleasure; but whether from pleasure or from sorrow (mixed as they are in the twisted strings of a man's heart, or a woman's), great tears fell from my stupid eyes, even on the blots of Lorna's.

output.summary: It follows from the position of the organs that if the proboscis of a dead humble-bee, or a thick bristle or rough needle, be pushed down the corolla, first of one form and then of the other, as an insect would do in visiting the two forms growing mingled together, pollen from the long-stamened form adheres round the base of the object, and is left with certainty on the stigma of the long-styled form; whilst pollen from the short stamens of the long-styled form adheres a little way above the extremity of the object, and some is generally left on the stigma of the other form. In accordance with this observation I found that the two kinds of pollen, which could easily be recognised under the microscope, adhered in this manner to the proboscides of the two species of humble-bees and of the moth, which were caught visiting the flowers; but some small grains were mingled with the larger grains round the base of the proboscis, and conversely some large grains with the small grains near the extremity of the proboscis. But to make my experiments perfectly fair, and to avoid any evil result from self-fertilisation or too close interbreeding, I have invariably employed pollen from a distinct plant of the same form for the illegitimate unions of all the species; and therefore it may be observed that I have used the term "own-form pollen" in speaking of such unions.

question: What insects did Darwin observe pollinating the Cowslip?
final_answer: Darwin recorded that the cowslip (Primula veris) was pollinated by **humble-bees**—specifically **Bombus hortorum** and **Bombus muscorum**—and also by a **moth**, **Cucullia verbasci**, which was caught visiting the flowers.

In accordance with this observation I found that the two kinds of pollen, which could easily be recognised under the microscope, adhered in this manner to the proboscides of the two species of humble-bees and of the moth, which were caught visiting the flowers; but some small grains were mingled with the larger grains round the base of the proboscis, and conversely some large grains with the small grains near the extremity of the proboscis. But to make my experiments perfectly fair, and to avoid any evil result from self-fertilisation or too close interbreeding, I have invariably employed pollen from a distinct plant of the same form for the illegitimate unions of all the species; and therefore it may be observed that I have used the term "own-form pollen" in speaking of such unions.

question: What does Shang Li do after he discovers Mulan is a woman?
gold: He sets her free because she saved his life fighting Shan Yu.
final_answer: After Shang Li realizes Mulan is a woman, he goes to her with his sword drawn—but instead of harming her, he throws the sword down in front of her and says, “A life for a life. My debt is repaid.” Then he turns away, orders the troops to “move out,” and marches on to the Imperial City, leaving Mulan behind.

question: Why did Burke release the face huggers on Newt and Ellen?
gold: To reproduce with them, and smuggle the embryos into Earth's quarantine.
final_answer: Burke did it so Ripley and Newt would be **impregnated with alien embryos**, letting him **smuggle the embryos back past quarantine**. As Ripley explains, if they were “impregnated… and then frozen for the trip back at just the right time,” **“nobody would know about the embryos”** they were carrying—allowing Burke to bring an alien back despite quarantine restrictions.

question: How did Ellen win the final showdown with the Alien Queen?
gold: She used the exosuit ladder to expel the queen into an airlock in outer space.
final_answer: Ripley fights the Alien Queen using the Sulaco’s **power loader**, striking it with the loader’s **cutting torch**, then drags/maneuvers the Queen into a **vertical loading airlock**. She **overrides the inner door** (latching the hold/lock) and hits **“OUTER DOOR OPEN,”** causing explosive decompression that **sucks the Queen out into space**, ending the showdown.

question: What does Madame de Carigliano believe about marriage that shocks Theodore?
final_answer: Madame de Carigliano says that “conjugal happiness has in all times been a speculation, a business demanding particular attention,” treating marriage as a practical “business” rather than a matter of passion—an attitude that shocks Theodore.

question: Who is Theodore de Summervieux?
final_answer: Theodore de Sommervieux is a young, publicly recognized painter (an artist “whose name … fame had stamped on Augustine’s heart”), who becomes Augustine Guillaume’s lover (and courtship interest). He is socially elevated enough to attend fashionable balls and tries—largely unsuccessfully because of the strict Guillaume household—to gain access to Augustine and communicate with her.

question: What causes Anvhar to have such extreme temperatures?
final_answer: Anvhar has such extreme temperatures because of its **unusual, highly elongated (“high‑angled sweeping cometary”) orbit**: for most of its **780‑day year** it arcs far out from its sun (bringing a long, intense winter), then returns closer in for only a **brief, very hot summer (about eighty days)** before plunging back outward again.

question: Why does Stew punch Bingy?
final_answer: Stew punches Bingy because Bingy needles him about becoming “Anne Schuyler’s husband” and even suggests Stew should sign his writing as **“Anne Schuyler’s Husband,”** implying Stew will be reduced to a pseudonymous appendage of Anne. Right before the punch, Bingy taunts him along those lines (e.g., “how does the old Cinderella man feel about that?”), and Stew hits him in response.
